item.description:
Search finds filenames throughout the current folder and its subfolders, with
wildcard and regular-expression support. File panes keep using the full window,
and folder entry and window closing follow predictable keyboard behavior.

### What's new

- Search (⌘F) always includes subfolders. Filename patterns such as `*.md`
  work directly; the optional Regex switch accepts expressions such as
  `\.(md|txt)$`. Plain text finds part of a filename. Typing directly in a
  pane keeps the live current-folder filter.
- Search results show each item's containing folder. Loading, empty, failed,
  and results states fill the available pane height.
- Search becomes available after the destination folder loads successfully.
  If observation follows a renamed folder but fails before its new listing
  arrives, Search closes and discards results rooted at the old location.
- Entering a folder highlights `..`, so pressing Enter again returns to its
  parent and highlights the folder just left. Typing a filter moves the cursor
  to a matching item instead, including while the folder's first listing loads.
- ⌘W closes the window even when several tabs are open. Portside keeps running;
  Window → Portside reopens it. Close Tab remains in the File menu and tab strip.

### Known limitations

- Search matches filenames only, returns the first 200 matches, and stays on
  its starting volume. It does not follow symbolic links or descend into packages.
- Regex matching is case-insensitive by default; inline flags can change it.
  Invalid or excessively expensive expressions stop with an editable error.
- Search is unavailable on SFTP tabs while recursive remote search is deferred.
  Typing directly in an SFTP pane still filters its current folder.
